aboutIntro: Kojo is a West African platform connecting clients with nearby workers — plumbing, electrical work, construction, cleaning, gardening, computing — in Mali, Senegal, Burkina Faso and Côte d'Ivoire. It started from a simple observation: finding someone reliable for a specific job was hard, and paying from a distance meant trusting blindly.
contactIntro: A question about a job, a payment or your account? The Kojo team answers Monday to Saturday, by phone, WhatsApp or email. For a job already under way, open the conversation in the app first: the person you reach has the context there, and the exchange stays in writing.
contactHelpText: To speed things up, tell us your account address, the job reference if there is one, and what is blocking. Requests are answered within one working day; for a payment, keep the operator receipt to hand.
privacyIntro: This page summarises what personal data Kojo keeps, what deleting an account erases, how long each item is kept and how to exercise your rights.
privacyDataBody: Kojo keeps the data needed to connect people and to process payment: account details (email address, first and last name, phone, country, photo, bio, skills), jobs and proposals, messages, reviews, notifications, device tokens, support tickets and verification codes. A payment carries no identifying data: it holds an amount, a status and internal account identifiers. No data is sold or used for advertising.
privacyRetentionBody: Each item follows a retention period the database enforces itself: verification code 10 minutes, payment left pending 48 hours, revoked token 24 hours, notification 90 days, deleted account 90 days before final purge, support ticket 365 days, message 730 days. A completed payment is never purged, for accounting reasons — it contains no identifying data.
privacyRightsBody: You can request a copy of your data and the deletion of your account from the app. Deletion anonymises the account: email address, password, first and last name, bio, phone, payment details and photo are erased, published jobs are closed and lose their location, and the account name is removed from notifications the other party already received. Messages stay: they belong to their recipient as well.
privacyContactBody: To exercise these rights or ask a question, write to the Kojo team from the contact page. The request is handled as a support ticket, and the reply says what was done.
homeAboutText1: Kojo grew out of an everyday problem in West Africa: finding a worker you can trust for a specific job, then paying them without travelling. The platform now brings together plumbers, electricians, masons, cleaners, gardeners and IT specialists in Mali, Senegal, Burkina Faso and Côte d'Ivoire, with verifiable profiles and reviews left after each completed job.
homeAboutText2: Every job is framed: the client posts the need, receives proposals, picks a worker, and the amount is held in escrow until the work is finished. The worker is paid by mobile money or card, without having to ask. A disagreement is handled inside the app, with the job history in front of both parties. Kojo can be reached Monday to Saturday by phone, WhatsApp or email, and support follows every job through to its close.

howItWorksHero: Find a worker or a job in West Africa, with total confidence, thanks to Kojo's secured payment.
howStep1Desc: The client describes their job (plumbing, electrical, mechanics, construction…) with a budget. Qualified workers in the area apply in seconds from their phone.
howStep2Desc: The client picks the right worker and pays via Orange Money, Wave or bank card. The money is held on Kojo's secured account: neither the client nor the worker can touch it before the job is done.
howStep3Desc: When the job is finished, the client validates and the money is paid out automatically to the worker. Simple, transparent, no disputes or surprises.
escrowWhatText: When you pay on Kojo, the money is not sent directly to the worker. It is held on a secured account (the escrow) until the job is done. Only after your validation is the amount released to the worker.
escrowGuarantee1: ✅ The client pays once, upfront — no risky cash payments.
escrowGuarantee2: ✅ The worker is certain to be paid at the end.
escrowGuarantee3: ✅ If cancelled before it starts, automatic refund.
escrowGuarantee4: ✅ The Kojo commission is shown before every payment.
faq1a: Escrow protects both sides: the client is sure the money is only released once the job is done, and the worker is sure to be paid. It's the trust guarantee most platforms lack.
faq2a: Orange Money (Senegal, Mali, Burkina Faso, Côte d'Ivoire), Wave (Senegal, Côte d'Ivoire) and bank card.
faq3a: As soon as the client validates the completed job, the escrowed amount (minus the Kojo commission, shown before payment) is paid out automatically to the worker's mobile money account.
faq4q: What happens if there is a problem?
faq4a: The payment stays locked until the job is validated. In case of disagreement, the Kojo team steps in via support. If a job is cancelled before it starts, the client is refunded automatically.
faq5a: Yes: French, English, Wolof, Bambara and Mooré. Everyone can use the app in their own language.
